subject: Post-demo shortlisted engines & business case
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@acmehealth.ai>, Dan Patel <dan.patel@acmehealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Sep 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo shortlisted engines & business case

Thanks again for the demo today — great conversation and lots of clarity on the clinical QA flows you want to protect in the POC. Short recap and a recommended shortlist with rationale below so the team can align before we send the formal commercial packet.

Quick recap
- Goal: 8-week POC to validate extraction + answer-over-EMR workflows for triage accuracy and hallucination rate <= 2% on the clinical prompt set we saw today.
- Success metrics: F1 for entity extraction, hallucination rate on closed prompts, 99th%-tile token latency under 250ms for interactive review workflows.

Shortlist (recommended for POC) — tradeoffs (cost / median latency / estimated quality)
1) redwood-open-7Q (quantized 7B) — Best cost baseline
   - Cost: ~$0.0025 / gen-token (hosted estimate)
   - Median token latency: ~40–60 ms (hosted, single-AZ)
   - 99th %-tile: ~120–160 ms (depends on sequence length; KV cache helps)
   - Quality: strong for structured extraction and high prompt throughput; lower for long-form clinical synthesis vs bigger models.

2) redwood-rt-13B (realtime-13B) — balanced latency and accuracy
   - Cost: ~$0.007 / gen-token
   - Median latency: ~70–95 ms
   - 99th %-tile: ~200–280 ms
   - Quality: noticeably better on nuanced clinical prompts and multi-hop reasoning; recommended when hallucination sensitivity is high.

3) large-guard-33B (accuracy-focused) — fallback for tough edge cases
   - Cost: ~$0.018 / gen-token (higher)
   - Median latency: ~140–200 ms
   - 99th %-tile: ~350–450 ms
   - Quality: best on rare long-form clinical synthesis and safety-critical clarifications; use as conditional fallback for golden-path checks.

Why this slate
- Cost-first baseline (7Q) + one mid-tier (13B) + high-accuracy fallback gives you an operational path to tune cost vs safety.
- We recommend starting POC with 7Q + 13B active routing (smart routing by prompt type) and enable the 33B fallback only for flagged prompts to contain cost.

Attachments & artifacts I’m sharing
- acme_benchmarks_q3.csv (benchmarks from our internal sim on your prompt set)
- prompt_pack_acme_v1.zip (seed prompts + automated eval harness)
- commercial_proposal_ACME.pdf (initial pricing and pilot terms)

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Confirm the two sample datasets we should load into the eval harness (redacted, PHI-free).
2) Security contact to share SOC2 questionnaire & evidence (we’ll prepare an audit log export example).
3) Confirm decision on routing strategy (start with 7Q + 13B with 33B fallback?) by Wed 9/22 so we can provision sandbox seats.
4) If agreed, we’ll schedule an SRE enablement call (30m) and send a 1-page MOU for the 8-week pilot.

I’ll stand up a short eval job for your prompts and share a quick dashboard tomorrow. Attached the benchmark CSV + prompt pack for your team to scan.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Appreciate the rapid follow-up and the clear slate. A few clarifying Qs from our side:
- Can you confirm 99th%-tile latency numbers with the dataset size we discussed (avg sequence 800 tokens)? Our reviewers need to understand tail behavior under interactive load.
- For the per-token costs: is there a hosted vs dedicated delta we should budget for? Do you have an example monthly run-rate for ~500k gen-tokens/day for the two-tier routing (7Q primary, 13B conditional)?
- Security: we need SOC2 Type II evidence and an example audit log export (especially token-level tracing and retention controls). Is that available on hosted, or only on Dedicated/Private?
- Prompt pack: thanks — can your team mark which prompts exercise hallucination checks vs extraction checks? Want to prioritize the evaluation.

If you can get numbers by EOD tomorrow that’d be ideal. Also looping Dan on procurement timelines.

—Olivia
Head of Clinical AI | Acme Health
olivia@acmehealth.ai | (617) 555-1248

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Sep 2027 17:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo shortlisted engines & business case

Thanks — answering inline and attaching a short run-rate table.

On 99th%-tile latency (avg seq ~800 tokens)
- redwood-open-7Q: 99th%-tile ~150–210 ms (single AZ, warmed KV cache; depends on concurrent user spikes).
- redwood-rt-13B: 99th%-tile ~260–320 ms.
- large-guard-33B: 99th%-tile ~380–480 ms.
Notes: our runtime’s continuous batching and KV caching significantly compress p99 for short interactive requests; for ~800-token sequences, we expect p99 to rise vs micro-benchmarks above — the numbers above reflect our simulated load using your prompt shapes (attached CSV).

Cost and run-rate (hosted example, rough daily gen tokens = 500k) — high level
- Baseline (7Q primary; 13B fallback for 15% of requests): ~ $14k/month hosted (gen-token cost + request overhead).
- Mid-tier (13B primary; 33B fallback for 5%): ~ $38k/month hosted.
- Dedicated: expect 20–35% lower per-token unit cost at committed throughput, but add monthly reserved capacity (depends on VM/GPU sizing). I’ll have a dedicated cost worksheet if you’re considering committed capacity.

Security / SOC2 / audit logs
- Hosted: Redwood is SOC2 Type II compliant; we can provide the SOC2 report under NDA and an example audit-log export (token-level access logs + per-request metadata).
- Dedicated/Private: provides customer-controlled retention and optional HSM/KMS for keys. If you need full VPC isolation and longer retention windows, Dedicated is the path.

Prompt pack labeling
- I’ve annotated prompt_pack_acme_v1.zip: folder /hallucination_checks and /extraction_checks. The eval harness includes scripts to run both suites and produce a hallucination-rate report.

Next steps (recommended)
1) Confirm POC scope + sample dataset by 9/22.
2) We’ll run a 24–48h smoke eval (our infra) and share a p50/p90/p99 latency + hallucination dashboard.
3) If green, we’ll issue the MOU and provision a sandbox org (hosted) for the 8-week pilot.

Attaching: acme_benchmarks_q3.csv (annotated), pilot_runrate_estimates.xlsx (summary).

Happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow to walk the numbers with Dan/procurement.

—Marissa
